A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PMATIC research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across restructuring.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 1 report original compression and synthetic-mismatch decoding experiments using Llama 3.1 on two Wikipedia datasets.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.4 report original compression benchmarks, helper-bit measurements, cross-device decoding tests and mismatch analyses.

M1.justification: The main PMATIC encoder, decoder, quantization and helper-bit procedure remain unchanged. However, v1's Section 4.2 footnote describes an optional PRNG-based random translation of bins to avoid the uniformity assumption; this procedural extension is omitted in v2. Neither version reports evaluating that extension.

E1.justification: v2 retains the two Wikipedia datasets and adds Hamlet, Emma, French Candide and Chinese Dream of the Red Chamber, substantially extending text-domain and language coverage. It also adds actual cross-device prediction mismatch as a test scenario beyond synthetic perturbations.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates gzip and matched non-robust arithmetic coding. v2 Table 1 retains these comparisons and adds cmix, brotli, bzip2, xz and zstd, including on the original datasets. cmix was previously cited but not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v2 adds Mistral 7B and Qwen2.5 7B configurations, a third robustness setting, and an M2 Pro/M4 Max decoding protocol using 100 Wikipedia articles and 50 Emma files of 5 KB. The existing 512-token context and 256-token truncation remain unchanged. The third setting is inconsistently stated: Section 5 says δ = 0.1, whereas Tables 1–2 and the robustness results use δ = 0.01.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's two synthetic-noise settings, v2 tests real hardware mismatch and adds substantial diagnostic analysis. Table 2 checks the helper-bit uniformity assumption and storage overhead; Appendix A.4 adds a mismatch histogram, exploration of relationships with token probability, and decoded-output failure cases.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or formal significance-testing procedures. v2's helper-bit averages and mismatch histogram add descriptive findings without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive compression scores and helper-bit measurements, plus successful cross-device decoding of all 150 files at δ = 0.01 versus none with arithmetic coding or δ = 0.001. Shared Llama compression ratios are retained. However, gzip's Wikipedia ratio changes from 40.88% to 47.59%; equivalent settings are unestablished because only v2 specifies level 9. v1's bits-per-token, bits-per-character and compressed-byte entries are omitted.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 supplies a full calculus derivation of the maximization yielding tanh(ε/2), a step asserted without derivation in v1's Proposition 1. The conditional-TV definition, proposition, correctness theorem and compression-loss bound remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of model-agnostic robust coding, correctness and favorable compression remain. Section 1.3 replaces v1's broad claim to first address prediction mismatch as a fundamental obstacle with the narrower claim of providing the first proof of concept using robust coding algorithms.

C2.justification: v2 explains low helper-bit frequencies through probabilities near zero or one and identifies better helper-bit probability estimation as an improvement opportunity. Appendix A.4 distinguishes observed decoding success from guarantees when mismatch bounds are exceeded and hypothesizes that quantization-bin jumps explain immediate failures at insufficient tolerance. Section 6 develops the implications of stochastic mismatch beyond v1's general future-work suggestion.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies Llama's 4-bit quantization, the added models' 3-bit quantization and vocabulary sizes, baseline compression levels, MIT Supercloud, and the laptop chipsets and GPU core counts. Existing context-window and llama-zip implementation information is retained across relocation. Some original corpus counts and exact size information are omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted discussion of Hu and Tang's concurrent Huffman-like mismatch-resistant method and deterministic inference work by He and Lab and Yuan et al., positioning the latter as complementary. It also adds the Supercloud reference and adjusts the novelty claim; the broader related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: The six-section main structure and most introductory, algorithmic and proof prose are retained. Changes include local language edits, 'longform' terminology, reorganized experimental subsections, implementation details moved into Appendix A.3, acknowledgments moved before references, and numbered technical appendix subsections.

P2.justification: v1's compact results display, labeled Figure 1, becomes a substantially redesigned model-by-dataset Table 1. v2 also adds a helper-bit table, two explanatory diagrams, a mismatch histogram and colored decoding-example panels. The new worked example contains a labeling error: Figure 2 assigns bitstring 010 to both A and E.

improvement.justification: v1 explicitly left real-world mismatch validation unresolved. v2's 150-file cross-device experiment addresses that central empirical gap and demonstrates a practical benefit over matched arithmetic coding. Broader languages, models and stronger baselines substantially strengthen the evidence, while the appendix proof and diagnostics clarify the reasoning and limitations. These gains outweigh localized reporting problems, including the inconsistent robustness parameter, duplicated bitstring in Figure 2 and omitted corpus details. Real-device evidence remains limited to one hardware pair.
